reviews.comment: Very good lectures, overall very good class.

reviews.comment: Prof Makowicki is one of my favorite professors thus far. Be prepared to read the textbook as a lot of the deeper explanations to his test questions are from that, but the questions can all be answered from notes. Great, interesting lectures. If you do the reading and stay on top of the class, you'll do good.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are start to finish for every single class period; they do not go strictly in a chronological order so it's a little hard to follow. TONS of material on each exam. He is very knowledgeable but comes off cocky. Interesting material, but not an easy A, even with a lot of studying. MUST ATTEND CLASS to have info for test.

If you aren't afraid of doing some work in a college class, you'll do fine. Come to class, do the reading, take notes. He is very accessible outside of class if you need help. Not an easy A but you'll learn and be a better writer.

I do not recommend this class if you just need a history credit. This class is challenging to do well in. 16 weeks of lecture into 2 tests SO hard, no study guide, review or practice exam. And a term paper he grades like an English prof. His lectures are extremely long. He is a nice guy and is very knowledgeable but his expectations are ridiculous.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing prof. Interested in subject, lectures on cool topics, and interacts with the class. Note that you do have to show up to class or at least get notes from a peer to get important info. There is also a textbook and 2 other books required, but they're manageable and definitely not too much to handle. Don't procrastinate on the reading.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mr. Makowiki is a solid prof. But it's impossible to be sure what you're going to be tested on. There are only two exams, the midterm and the final, so get ready to study months of lectures and read tens of chapters if you want to make high marks in this class. I found the class interesting but I would not take it again.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You will not regret this Professor or his Class. The lectures are very methodically made and he actually provides tons of interesting knowledge beyond the slides. I highly recommend that if you can take Prof. Mackowiki, you do it! If you are taking his History of American Seapower course JUST REMEMBER THAT THE EXAMS TEST ON NAMES AND DATES!
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Outstanding lectures that I enjoyed hearing; material was fun and interesting. Just read the textbook, take notes in lectures, and you'll do fine. Be aware that it's synchronous, i.e. no posted lecture recordings or slides. Also be sure to start the primary source reading early, as there's only one paper and a good bit of material for it.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He grades the one essay in this class pretty harshly, so be prepared. It was an interesting class, but I wish the way each grade was worth wasn't so punishing. I felt like studying didn't prepare me for the exam, since it was difficult to know what he wanted us to take away from each lecture.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His lectures are actually very engaging and I hate history. He does assign an essay over two books you have to read. The quizzes are really easy and the tests are straight from the lecture material. Definitely helps to read the textbook though.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Makowicki knows his history and teaches the learning material easily. Take notes and read the books and you will have an easy A. Little to no homework. 2-3 quizzes and a couple exams that relate to the notes and books as well as one essay. He also seriously cares about your success in writing and wants the best out of you.
